text:
mina: Hey infra team — planning to add a new mixed GPU nodepool in asia-northeast3 for low-latency embeddings. Thinking L4 nodes for interactive requests + A10G for bulk embed jobs. Quotas look tight on accelerators. Anyone see obvious pitfalls for sizing and autoscaler settings?

rajeev: +1 on splits. First check: project GPU quota and regional VCPU quota. asia-northeast3 often has low accelerator quota. I can file a request but need the exact SKU counts.

mina: Thanks, rajeev. Initial ask: 6 L4 (1 GPU each) + 8 A10G (1 GPU each) as a start. We’ll tune later.

sam: For that workload I'd do two nodepools: 
- lp-lowlatency-l4: minNodes=1, maxNodes=4, use compact machine (4 vcpu/16g) to keep latency down
- hp-throughput-a10: minNodes=0, maxNodes=8, larger machine (16 vcpu/64g) for batching.

Also recommend: cluster-autoscaler flags: --scale-down-unneeded-time=10m, --scale-down-delay-after-add=15m, --balance-similar-node-groups=true. Prevents immediate teardown and eviction storms.

sam: Example nodepool spec we used elsewhere: 
```yaml
nodePool:
  name: lp-lowlatency-l4
  machineType: n1-highmem-4
  accelerators:
    - type: nvidia-l4
      count: 1
  taints:
    - key: "gpu-type"
      value: "l4"
      effect: "NoSchedule"
  autoscaling:
    minNodeCount: 1
    maxNodeCount: 4
```

mina: Nice. Any suggestions for pod config? I want the embed service to prefer L4 but fallback to A10G if congested.

ellie: Use nodeAffinity + tolerations and a preferredDuringScheduling affinity for L4. Also expose a runtime hint env var so the app can switch batch size based on GPU type.

ellie: Quick pod snippet: 
```yaml
affinity:
  nodeAffinity:
    preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
      - weight: 100
        preference:
          matchExpressions:
            - key: gpu-type
              operator: In
              values: [l4]
tolerations:
  - key: "gpu-type"
    operator: "Exists"
    effect: "NoSchedule"
```

rajeev: One operational gotcha — driver/runtime mismatch. L4 prefers CUDA 12.x runtime; some A10G AMIs we have use CUDA 11.7. If you mix node images, ensure container runtime and driver versions are compatible, or use the NVIDIA device plugin with matching driver. We had a node leak last month from driver plugin OOM.

ops-oncall: also watch for quota interplay: GPUs are limited but the cluster autoscaler needs vCPU and IP addresses quotas too. If nodepool requests hit subnet IP limits, pods will Pending even when GPU quota is available.

mina: Good call. I’ll add a preflight checklist: 1) request accelerator quota for region 2) verify vCPU and subnet IPs 3) prepare AMIs with matching drivers 4) create minimal nodepool terraform plan.

sam: Cost tradeoff: L4 instances are cheaper per-hour but less memory; keep batch size conservative to avoid OOM. For heavy batches prefer A10G. Consider reserved A10G capacity (dedicated) if throughput is stable — cuts per-token cost ~25% compared to on-demand.

infra-bot: Quota request ticket created: Q-2026-3932 for asia-northeast3 accelerator quota increase (6 L4 + 8 A10G). ETA ~48-72h.

ops-oncall: One more ops note: set PodPriority classes — high for interactive embed service, lower for backend batch ingestion. That way the autoscaler preemption order is sane when node pressure hits. Also add disruption budgets for the interactive pods.

mina: Thanks everyone. Action items: rajeev files quota (done by infra-bot), ellie will bake AMI with CUDA 12, sam will draft the terraform nodepool + autoscaler flags, ops-oncall will add priority classes + PDBs. I’ll wait for quota before applying. :thumbsup:

ops-oncall: If quota gets delayed, fallback plan: spin a small Dedicated A10G reserved pool in us-west4 and route non-latency traffic there until asia quota comes in.

mina: noted. I’ll update this thread after quota confirmation.
